figure1.prompt:
Create a publication-quality academic scientific teaser diagram for an ICML mechanistic interpretability paper. This is a NEW portrait figure. Aspect ratio exactly 3:4, white background, very sharp typography, intended to occupy a single column 3.25 inches wide. Use the supplied accepted-paper pages ONLY as stylistic references: thin black/gray outlines, pale muted blue/green/lavender fills, Times New Roman / serif labels, compact clear academic panels, modest arrows, no decorative shadows, no bulky modern infographic cards. Do not reproduce reference scientific content. All labels must remain readable at single-column size: large panel titles and medium-size body text, generous white space between objects, no tiny footnotes.

Three vertically stacked panels, clearly marked (a), (b), (c), occupying approximately 38%, 30%, 32% of image height. Thin horizontal dividers, no enclosing heavy border.

(a) Panel title EXACT: "Correct hops, failed composition".
Under it, a small gray label "Same ten-paragraph context". Then a compact knowledge chain across the width: a pale-blue box with text "Walter II\nof Avesnes", a right arrow labeled "father", a pale-blue box "James\nof Avesnes", a right arrow labeled "died in", a pale-green box "Arsuf". Split words onto lines exactly as needed for readability. Below chain, two small green checks with labels "Hop 1: James" and "Hop 2: Arsuf". Under these print the question on two centered lines: "Where did Walter's father die?" Then a coral-tinted answer strip "Native: Avesnes" with a red X. This depicts a real test example.

(b) Panel title EXACT: "Access and reading interact".
A small document glyph at left labeled "Bridge paragraph", with a purple location marker and adjacent label "Address recoverable".
Below this place two equal-sized pale-color boxes side by side, connected by a double-headed dark arrow:
left pale-blue box text "Paragraph\naccess"
right pale-lavender box text "Local\nreading".
Above the connecting double-headed arrow, small label "interaction".
The document connects down to both boxes with thin neutral arrows. This is a functional interaction, with no layer numbers or exclusive anatomical stages. No numerical plots.

(c) Panel title EXACT: "Mechanistic repair".
A horizontal small row: two document glyphs labeled "Root" and "Selected bridge", connected by a slim arrow to a stylized small attention-head grid where a few cells are teal and the rest gray. Label under grid "CoReTrace (Ours)". A small line above grid "Select evidence + adapt heads".
Below this row a large pale-teal answer strip "Composed answer: Arsuf" with a teal check.
At bottom a compact bold serif takeaway: "Correct composition from the input".

Color palette: text near-black #20252B; ours and success teal #087F8C; pale teal #E5F2EF; failure coral #D76B50 with pale fill #F5EBE6; address signal purple #6F5AA8 with pale fill #EEEAF5; neutral baseline gray #8C959F, pale gray #F0F1F2. Keep all surfaces matte and flat. No overall figure title, no caption, no logo, no statistical chart, no textual exclusions or disclaimers. All text exactly spelled and compact.
style_references: 2025.acl-long.196_Interpret and Improve In-Context Learning via the Lens of Input-Label.pdf, p.1

figure2.prompt:
Create a NEW academic mechanism/method framework figure for an ICML paper. Landscape aspect ratio 2.2:1. White background. It will span 6.75 inches at print size. Use accepted-paper framework references for stylistic guidance ONLY and use the third reference portrait teaser as this paper's precise typography/color style. Design must look like a careful scientific framework: thin black/gray outlines, Times-like serif body labels, bold serif panel headings, restrained italic annotations, flat pale colored areas. Avoid shadows, decorative clipart, heavy pill headers, and huge blank areas. All text sharply readable.

TWO horizontal rows separated by a thin gray line, with black serif title at upper left of each:
"(a) Mechanism-guided preparation"
"(b) Evidence-guided inference"

TOP ROW has three clear equal-width modules in adjacent pale regions:
LEFT module title "Locate evidence-access heads". Inside show two small document/question symbols at left labeled "Direct hop" and "Composed query"; a slim arrow into a small attention-head grid with 3 teal cells and the rest gray. Under grid put "Paired paragraph-attention gap".
CENTER module title "Adapt selected heads". Inside four equal-sized boxes labeled "Q", "K", "V", "O". ALL FOUR BOXES are identically pale teal with thin teal border, explicitly indicating all four projections are trained. Below print "Composed-answer training". Under that a small light-gray strip "Fixed native V/O restoration". Add a small note "Selected prefill positions" beneath the strip.
RIGHT module title "Fit the address readout". Small line "Adapted-model attention features". Under this the simple exact formula "s(p) = wᵀ h(p)" in a pale purple rectangle, with arrows toward three paragraph glyphs. Under print "Training bridge supervision".
A thin teal arrow connects CENTER to RIGHT, labelled "state-aligned features" in small but readable type.

BOTTOM ROW is a compact left-to-right inference workflow, not a tree of anatomical stages:
At FAR LEFT a stack of small documents plus a question mark, with label "Context + question".
Arrow to a small directed title-link graph with one teal root and two coral/light-blue candidate nodes, label "Title-link candidates".
Then a three-branch vertical selector column, all labels clearly spelled:
top pale green box "One: use candidate"
middle pale purple box "Several: attention readout"
bottom pale gray box "Empty: retain context".
Top and middle branch converge into two original document glyphs labeled "Root + bridge".
Arrow from those documents to a teal outlined rectangular model box labeled "Scoped head adaptation".
The bottom 'Empty: retain context' branch bypasses the two-document glyphs and goes directly into that same model box using a thin neutral gray arrow.
Arrow from model box to a small light-teal rounded rectangle "Answer".
Maintain clear left-to-right arrow direction and avoid crossings.

Two dashed carry-over links from TOP ROW:
1. Teal dashed arrow from "Adapt selected heads" downward to the "Scoped head adaptation" model box.
2. Purple dashed arrow from "Fit the address readout" downward to ONLY the middle "Several: attention readout" selector box. Route these along the row-divider corridor with enough separation so they do not intersect text.
No other vertical arrows.

Bottom compact line in neutral black serif: "Input-derived selection • Original paragraph text • Greedy answer generation".
Do NOT add exclusions, 'not', 'no support labels', footnotes, a caption, a figure number, a logo, any statistics plot, or layer-by-layer causal claims.
Palette exact: near-black #20252B; teal #087F8C with pale #E5F2EF; coral #D76B50 pale #F5EBE6; purple #6F5AA8 pale #EEEAF5; gray #8C959F pale #F0F1F2. Layout polished, compact and aligned; same visual family as portrait teaser.
style_references: 2025.acl-long.196_Interpret and Improve In-Context Learning via the Lens of Input-Label.pdf, p.2
